title: DSA - Bucket Sort Time Complexity
description:
## Bucket Sort Analysis
Recall how bucket sort works:
1. Create k empty buckets
2. Distribute n elements into buckets based on value
3. Sort each bucket (usually with insertion sort)
4. Concatenate all buckets

### Best/Average Case: O(n + k)
When elements are **uniformly distributed** across buckets:
- Step 1: O(k) to create buckets
- Step 2: O(n) to distribute
- Step 3: Each bucket has ~n/k elements. Insertion sort on small lists is fast
- Step 4: O(k) to concatenate

### Worst Case: O(n²)
When ALL elements land in ONE bucket:
- You're just running insertion sort on the entire array
- This happens with non-uniform data

### Space: O(n + k)
You need the extra bucket storage.

### When to use bucket sort:
- Input is uniformly distributed across a known range
- You need better than O(n log n)
- Extra memory is acceptable

### Comparison:
| Algorithm | Best | Average | Worst | Space | In-place? |
|-----------|------|---------|-------|-------|-----------|
| Quicksort | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n²) | O(1) | Yes |
| Merge Sort | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n log n) | O(n) | No |
| Bucket Sort | O(n + k) | O(n + k) | O(n²) | O(n + k) | No |

---
## Question:
You have 1 million uniformly distributed floats between 0 and 1. Which sort is fastest?
b1t: Quicksort - O(n log n) average, in-place
b2t: Merge sort - guaranteed O(n log n)
b3t: Bucket sort - O(n + k) with uniform distribution
